angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 3,973,143 km at 52.25 pc = 1.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 115623: distance 52.247 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.009), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 52.247 +/- 0.47 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 18.7061 +/- 0.1356 mas (same row, RUWE 1.05), 137.9 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 5.711 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 115623: radius 5.711 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 37.449 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.043) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 3,973,143 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 5979 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 115623: effective temperature 5979 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.053) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 115623: effective temperature 5979 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.053) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 1115) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 3.32 from 2023ApJS..266...41P; the 4 published values span log g 2.918 to 4.39, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.6% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJS..266...41P)
